$schema_note: Machine-readable fixture manifest for the Whyfile conformance corpus. Each entry: id, rule_id (the CORPUS rule number), spec_rule_ids (the rule ids in the normative spec that this fixture exercises -- corpus numbering is independent of the spec's, so reconcile through this field, never by matching numbers), family, rule_statement, valid, kind (record | record_dir | filename_scenario | vector | envelope), path (relative to this manifest's directory), verdict_kind, expect, notes. THE VERDICT LIVES IN `verdict_kind` + `expect` AND NOWHERE ELSE: a harness must be able to decide every fixture without reading `notes` or any other prose. `valid` alone is not a verdict -- it does not distinguish 'must not parse at all' from 'is the counter-example for this rule'. verdict_kind values: `parse_rejects` (the input must not parse as a record at all); `field_expectation` (it parses, and `expect` names the required field values); `envelope_shape` (`expect` names `conformant`, the `command` tag, `required_keys`, `forbidden_keys`, and `constraints`, or for a counter-example the `violates` rule ids and the `failing_condition`); `vector` (`expect.compare_fields` names the fields in the fixture file that carry the expected output); `filename_scenario` (`expect.filename` is the destination the scenario must resolve to; on a counter-example `expect.conformant_filename` is what a conformant implementation produces instead). REC-family entries additionally carry `spec_rules`: the rule id(s) in the normative spec text that the fixture exercises -- the corpus's own `rule_id` numbering is INDEPENDENT of the spec's and collides with it in the REC-001..REC-011 range, so `spec_rules` is the only safe key to compute spec coverage from. `verdict_kind` is `parse_rejects` (the input must not parse as a record at all) or `field_expectation` (it parses; the fields in `expect` must hold), and `expect` states the required outcome field by field so a harness can decide every fixture without reading prose. `reference_conforms: false` plus `divergence` and `reference_actual` marks a fixture whose `expect` states the SPEC-required outcome that the v0.8.3 reference implementation does NOT currently produce. Additional `kind` values used by the REC family: render_scenario, slug_scenario, identity_scenario.

rule_families.REC: Record format -- what makes a markdown file a decision record, and how its fields parse.
rule_families.FIL: Record filename scheme -- how a captured record's filename is chosen and matched over time. Renamed from VER after the two families collided; VER now means SPECIFICATION versioning and nothing else. In the normative spec these rules live under REC-056..REC-070.
rule_families.PROV: Provenance -- the trust-tier vocabulary and how it ranks/aggregates.
rule_families.ENV: Result envelope -- the per-command JSON shape returned by the CLI.
rule_families.VER: Specification versioning -- when a change to the format requires a version marker and a migration note, and what absence is allowed to mean afterwards.

rules.statement: A record's H1 MUST be `# ADR-<digits><sep><title>` (sep in em-dash/en-dash/colon/hyphen) or `# Decision: <title>`; any other H1 means the file is NOT a decision record.
A record MUST have a `## Decision` section (case-insensitive heading); its body becomes the rationale. Without it the file is not a record, even if the H1 gate passes.

A BOM (U+FEFF) is stripped only when it is the very FIRST character of the file. A BOM occurring elsewhere (e.g. immediately before a later heading) is left in place and is NOT treated as part of the heading gate.
`## Alternatives considered` (or `## Alternatives`) is OPTIONAL; when absent, `alternatives` MUST be an empty list, not an error.

Alternatives are parsed as a FLAT top-level list only (numbered `1.`/`2.` or bulleted `-`/`*`). Nested/indented sub-bullets are NOT attached to their parent item; each becomes its own separate flat list item.

Status comes from the inline `**Status:**` line when present; normalised to the first lowercase alphabetic word (tolerating trailing punctuation/clauses). A `## Status` section heading is used ONLY as a fallback when no inline `**Status:**` line exists -- if both are present, the inline line always wins.

A record whose normalised status is 'rejected' MUST be excluded from the authored/captured ground-truth node set built from a directory of records -- the option not taken must never become ground truth.

A `## Assumptions` list item MAY carry a `(review by YYYY-MM-DD)` clause and/or an `(expires: ...)` clause, both stripped from the claim text into separate `review_by`/`expiry` fields. A review-by date that is not in YYYY-MM-DD form is NOT extracted -- it stays embedded in the claim text.
An ADR H1's `ADR-<digits>` prefix and its separator are stripped from the parsed title; the title is the H1 text with that prefix removed, not the raw heading.

A `## Recommendation` section produces a `resolution_delta: {recommended, chosen}` field on the node ONLY when its text differs from the chosen/title text. When it is absent, or textually equal to the title, `resolution_delta` MUST be omitted entirely (never emitted as null/empty).

Supersession is recorded ONLY for the ACTIVE phrasing `supersedes ADR-<digits>` found anywhere in the record text. The passive phrasing `superseded by ADR-<digits>` MUST NOT be captured as an outgoing `supersedes` reference.
A brand-new captured record is named `YYYY-MM-DD-<question-slug>.md`. The slug MUST derive from the QUESTION text, never from the chosen option.

Re-capturing the SAME question on a later date MUST reuse the existing dated record file (whatever its own date), never create a second one. Reuse requires a well-formed 4-2-2 all-digit date prefix; a malformed prefix does not count as an existing dated record.

A pre-dated-scheme (legacy) filename `<chosen-slug>.md` is reused ONLY when the file's recorded `## Context` body matches the new question (whitespace/case-normalised). A legacy file recording a DIFFERENT question, even with an identical chosen-derived filename, MUST NOT be reused/overwritten.
A legacy-named file that cannot be recognised as a decision record at all (no parseable `## Context` section) MUST NEVER be treated as a match, regardless of filename.

The lookup for an existing dated record MUST use a digit-CLASS-anchored glob (`[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-<qslug>.md`), never an unanchored `*`-prefixed pattern -- `*` can match a short question's slug as a mere suffix of an unrelated, longer, older record's slug.

The digit-CLASS-anchored glob must also beat a `?`-positional pattern (`????-??-??-<qslug>.md`): `?` matches ANY character, not only digits, so it can mistake a legacy undated filename for a dated one when the legacy slug happens to be 'date-shaped' in its first 11 characters.

A new-scheme (question-derived) slug longer than 60 characters is truncated at a WORD boundary, never mid-word. (The separate LEGACY slug function intentionally hard-cuts at exactly 60 chars and must never be changed to match -- it exists only to reproduce old filenames byte-for-byte.)

Valid provenance tier values are exactly {authored, captured, attested, reconstructed}. Trust ranking, most to least trusted: authored < captured < attested < reconstructed (lower rank integer = more trusted).
A record whose H1 is `# ADR-...` ingests with provenance='authored'; a record whose H1 is `# Decision: ...` ingests with provenance='captured'. The two MUST map to different tiers.

A node with a missing/absent `provenance` key, an empty string, or any unrecognised value MUST rank/count identically to `reconstructed` (the lowest tier) -- never silently promoted to a trusted tier.

golden_fraction counts only nodes whose provenance is in {authored, captured, attested}; reconstructed (and absent-provenance) nodes never contribute to the golden numerator under any circumstance. An empty node list yields 0%, not an error.

Every command's JSON envelope MUST include a `command` key (the subcommand name) and a `status` key. These are the ONLY two keys guaranteed common to every command -- the envelope is a per-command tagged union, not one fixed shape.

The `why` command's envelope MUST carry {command, status, query, count, cutoff, score_stats, results}. It is NOT a closed key set: the reference implementation adds an eighth key, `note`, on the `topically_weak` status (verified by execution at v0.8.3), so a conformant validator MUST check for the required keys rather than assert an exact key set.
The `list-intent` command's envelope keys are EXACTLY {command, count, filter, intent, status}.

The `coverage` command's envelope keys are EXACTLY {command, status, authored_anchored_files, authored_anchored_symbols, code_files, code_symbols, dark_files, file_coverage_pct, files_with_intent, golden, intent_by_kind, intent_debt, symbol_coverage_pct, symbols_with_intent} (14 keys total).
The `check` command's envelope keys are EXACTLY {command, status, rules, files_checked, violations}.

`graph_identity` is NEVER part of the CLI's JSON envelope for any command. It is attached only by the MCP transport layer (mcp_server.py), and its presence or absence must never be used to satisfy or substitute for a command's real required-key set.
A query result MUST be a single JSON object -- not an array, not a stream of objects, not a bare value.

The envelope MUST be modelled as a tagged union discriminated by `command` over a universal core of {command, status}, NOT as one struct with every command's fields optional. A key that is not applicable to a variant MUST be omitted, never nulled.

Where one `command` value carries more than one disjoint shape, the secondary discriminator MUST be named and applied before any variant key is read. `coverage` is discriminated by the presence of `explain`; the two shapes share no key beyond `command` and `status`.

A failure envelope MUST carry `command`, `status` and a human-readable `message`, and MUST NOT be required to carry any variant-specific key. The error variant of every command is a legitimate shape with none of them.
Each entry in a `why` result set MUST carry all thirteen named fields, including the three evidence fields.
`alternatives` MUST be a list of strings. A legacy scalar MUST be coerced to a one-element list and MUST NOT be iterated character by character.
`matched_coverage` MUST be a number in [0, 1], and `distinctive_matches` MUST be a subset of `matched_terms` -- it is by definition the corpus-distinctive part of what matched.

`topically_weak` MUST mean an abstention ABOVE the cutoff: the top hit cleared the score threshold but its match evidence does not support treating it as an answer. It MUST NOT be read as equivalent to `ok`.
`weak_match` MUST mean the top result scored UNDER the cutoff but stands clearly apart from the runner-up -- a probable answer at moderate confidence, not noise.
Each entry in a `list-intent` result set MUST carry all nine named fields, including `confidence_score`.
The `explain` `ambiguous` variant MUST carry `candidates` and `message`, and MUST NOT carry `resolved`. An implementation MUST NOT silently pick a candidate.
A component of `intent_debt` the implementation cannot compute MUST be reported as an explicit null, never as 0. A zero claims a measurement that did not happen.

The `capture` envelope MUST carry all nine named keys. Both the as-given `record` path (from which node identity derives) and the resolved `record_abs` MUST be reported, and `resolution_delta` MUST be present with an explicit null when there is no delta.
The `changed` envelope MUST carry `base`, `changed_files`, `files_with_intent` and `results`; `ambiguous` MUST be true when a basename match resolves to more than one path.
The `digest` envelope MUST carry `since`, `added`, `removed` and `superseded`.
Each violation MUST cite the identifier of the decision it enforces. A rule whose failure cannot name its decision is a lint, not a conformance check.

A transport that attaches a credential block MUST attach it unconditionally, with an explicit null when nothing resolved, and the attached key MUST NOT collide with any key the specification assigns to a command variant.
Status tokens are per-command, not global; an honest-negative status is a complete answer rather than an error. A token belonging to another command MUST be treated as a failure.

A question that slugifies to the empty string MUST become the literal slug `decision`. It MUST NOT fall back to naming the record from the chosen option -- that reintroduces the collision class the question-derived scheme exists to kill.
A slug MUST be bounded at 60 characters, truncating on a word boundary; a first word that alone exceeds the bound is hard-cut, the only permitted mid-word cut.
An empty question MUST be treated as matching a recorded `## Context` of `(none recorded)`, and only that.

The `## Context` heading consulted when claiming a legacy record MUST be matched by the same rules as every other section heading -- case-insensitively and at any level -- but the recorded question MUST still be read and MUST still match.

An unrecognised provenance value -- not merely an absent one -- MUST rank identically to `reconstructed`. Matching is exact: `AUTHORED` is not `authored`, and an invented fifth tier is never promoted.
Trust ordering MUST use provenance as the primary sort key and numeric confidence only as the secondary one. A high-confidence `reconstructed` result MUST NOT outrank a low-confidence `authored` one.
Intent ingested from a decision record MUST carry a numeric confidence of exactly 1.0. The record is the evidence; trust is carried by provenance, on a separate axis.
A trust metric that blends tiers into a single scalar MUST also report the per-tier breakdown and the tier set it treated as trusted.

Absence means 'this was not recorded' and MUST keep meaning that. An implementation MUST NOT retroactively infer a value for a field a record does not carry, nor re-render the gap as an explicit null.

fixtures.rule_statement: Otherwise the destination MUST be `<today>-<question-slug>.md`.

DIVERGENCE: v0.8.3 substitutes the CHOSEN option for an empty question before slugging (`slugify(question.strip() or chosen)`) and emits `2026-07-25-keep-the-window.md` -- a chosen-derived filename, which is precisely the collision class REC-056 exists to kill.
